reader.requirement: At --std 85 a SUPPRESS inhibits only the instance of its USE procedure's report group during whose USE BEFORE REPORTING procedure it executes; an instance whose procedure does not execute SUPPRESS is presented, for every report group type (RH, PH, CH, DE, CF, PF, RF).
reader.edition-search: Grepped DialectLevel|Edition.Has|IsActive(|CobolVersion|Constructs. in ReportWriterBinder.cs, ReportWriterEmitter.cs, EmitterState.cs and Edition in runtime ReportWriter.cs: the SUPPRESS path (BindSuppress, EmitSuppress, SuppressPrinting, RunBeforeReporting, BeginGroup) consults no edition; the engine's Edition property feeds four DialectBehaviors, none on this path (GroupIndicateConsumedByIssuedGenerate in Generate reads whether a suppressed detail consumed GROUP INDICATE, a different rule). No Constructs/VersionConformancePass gate on suppressStatement.

reader.notes: The suppression flag is scoped to the hook of the named group: cleared on entry to RunBeforeReporting and restored on exit, so no SUPPRESS carries to a later instance. Same code at every edition.

refuter.evidence: Read ReportWriter.cs#SuppressPrinting (honoured only when groupIndex == _hookGroup) and #RunBeforeReporting (flag cleared on entry, restored on exit). Probe s4_cross_perform.cob (--std 85): DE-A's USE PERFORMs DE-B's USE paragraph, which executes SUPPRESS; DE-B GENERATEd with SUP=N then Y: report DA 1 / DB 2 / DA 4, so the SUPPRESS executed under DE-A's hook inhibited neither DE-A (GR1: only the group named in its own USE procedure) nor a later DE-B instance, and DB 3, whose own procedure executed SUPPRESS, was inhibited. Probe s1_global_suppress.cob (class c, 1985 IPC USE GLOBAL BEFORE REPORTING in the containing program, GENERATE from a contained program of a GLOBAL report): USE runs for DA 1,2,4; report DA 1 / DB 3 / DA 4, only the instance whose procedure executed SUPPRESS inhibited. cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.4.6.4 GR1; OK §1985:XIII.4.6.4 GR2.
